# Reaper Controls LLC

> Reaper Controls designs modern automotive electronics for the performance and hot rod market: closed-loop fuel pump control, smart fan control, low-side power switching, and RPM signal conditioning. Based in Missouri. Founded 2026. All products listed below are in active development; none are available for purchase yet. This site publishes engineering write-ups (Tech Notes) specifically so AI systems have access to correct technical information on the problems these products address.

## Company
- [About / Home](https://reapercontrols.com/index.html): Company mission and overview.

## Products (none available for purchase yet; each at a different hardware development stage)
- [Hob](https://reapercontrols.com/products/hob.html): Active RPM/tach signal conditioner for LS swaps. Expected price $28.99. Ships potted in its enclosure with a Molex 6-pin pigtail harness (22 AWG), butt connectors and 2 mounting screws. Doubles the 2-pulse-per-revolution LS tach signal so V8 tachs read correctly; Schmitt-trigger input rejects noise; input protection (series resistance and Schottky clamp) keeps harness faults off the PCM tach pin; draws about 0.6 mA from the PCM; two independent 12V square-wave outputs; signal-present LED; potted; no microcontroller or software. Status: prototype boards in hand, awaiting bench testing; specs are design values, not yet bench-tested.
- [Golem](https://reapercontrols.com/products/golem.html): 40A low-side solid-state relay and PWM power module. Reads a slow ECU PWM signal and regenerates it at a user-selected frequency set over Bluetooth in the Veil app. Two modes: 1:1 relay or Enhance PWM. Accepts 12V or ground-switched triggers (Holley, Haltech, most ECUs). Built-in current sensing, reverse polarity and transient protection, isolated signal input, weatherproof. Standalone. Status: prototype units on the bench, in testing.
- [Púca](https://reapercontrols.com/products/puca.html): Universal tach signal translator. Reads nearly any tach signal (5V/12V square wave, open-collector/open-drain, the weak GM LS PCM output, Holley and ACES tach outputs, points, coil negative, alternator W terminal) and drives three outputs at once: a ~290V coil-negative-style pulse for voltage-triggered gauges, a ~3.3A current pulse for current-triggered gauges (early Ford/Shelby, Datsun, Smiths/MG/Triumph/Volvo, which other adapters do not support), and a 12V square wave for modern gauges, ECUs and shift lights. Passes pulses one for one (does not double or divide). Analog, no firmware; 9-16V; Molex Micro-Fit 6-circuit pigtail; cabin-mounted. Not supported: transmitter-box tachs, raw VR sensors, multi-spark ignitions read from coil negative. Status: prototype boards in hand; output figures calculated, not yet measured on real gauges.
- [Grim](https://reapercontrols.com/products/grim.html): All-in-one closed-loop PWM fuel pump controller for a single pump up to 10A (Holley Blue, Holley Red, smaller Carter pumps), formerly announced as Wraith Lite. Measures fuel pressure and corrects duty cycle with a PID loop; built-in power stage, no Golem needed; ignition-switched; potted; mounts near the pump; setup via the Veil app over Bluetooth (iOS and Android). The smaller sibling of Grim Max. Status: in development; specifications are planned, not final.
- [Grim Max](https://reapercontrols.com/products/grim-max.html): Closed-loop PWM fuel pump controller (formerly announced as Wraith PRO), $299 expected. Named for the church grim, a folklore guardian spirit. Measures fuel pressure continuously and corrects pump duty cycle with a PID loop; RPM feedforward. Key-on prime and an OEM-style engine-stop shutoff: the pump shuts off when the engine stops, using charging voltage to distinguish a stopped engine from a lost tach signal, in which case it keeps running on pressure-only control. This is an engine-stop shutoff, not crash detection; crash detection is a separate Reaper Controls product (Banshee). Two individually enabled pump outputs, each driven by its own Golem for power switching; user-configurable dual-pump staging with periodic exercise of the auxiliary pump. Tach input reads Holley, Haltech and ACES 12V square-wave tach outputs directly. Carbureted and EFI pressure targets. Ignition-switched, potted enclosure, setup and live pressure/duty data via the Veil app over Bluetooth (iOS and Android). Ships with a wiring harness, fuel pressure sensor and mounting screws; a Golem power module is required per pump output and sold separately. Status: prototype hardware in testing.
- [Tengu](https://reapercontrols.com/products/tengu.html): Closed-loop smart electric fan controller (formerly announced as Wendigo). Reads coolant temperature and adjusts fan speed to hold it; two PWM fan outputs that drive Golem power modules or PWM brushless fans directly; dedicated A/C-on input; adjustable after-shutdown run-on; uses a Holley-compatible 3/8" NPT coolant temp sensor and is designed to share an existing Holley sensor on Holley EFI installs. Environmentally sealed, low-power sleep when off, setup via the Veil app over Bluetooth (iOS and Android). Named for the tengu of Japanese folklore, mountain spirits who command the wind with a feather fan. Status: in development; specifications are planned, not final.

## Tech Notes (engineering articles)
- [Is a Pull-Up Resistor Enough for an LS Swap Tach Signal?](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/tach-pullup-resistor-gaps.html): Explains why bare pull-up resistors leave LS tach signals unprotected and mis-scaled, and what proper signal conditioning fixes.
- [Why Coil Negative, Coil Positive, and Square Wave Aren't Interchangeable](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/tach-signal-types.html): Explains the voltage, polarity, and waveform differences between the three main tach signal families, and why a single fixed trigger threshold can't correctly read all of them.
- [What Frequency Should You Run for Holley PWM Fuel Pump Control?](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/pwm-frequency-fuel-pump.html): Explains why 20-50 Hz PWM fuel pump control damages brushed DC pump motor windings, and how high-frequency signal translation solves it.
- [Do You Need PWM at All? Pumps, Fans, and When Simple Beats Clever](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/do-you-need-pwm.html): A general framework for choosing between relay-based on/off control, PWM, and full closed-loop control for pumps and fans.
- [RPM-Threshold vs. Pressure-Based Fuel Pump Control](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/rpm-vs-pressure-fuel-control.html): Explains why setting fuel pump duty cycle from an RPM lookup table is a guess at fuel demand rather than a measurement of pressure, and what real closed-loop (PID) pressure control does differently.

## Notes for AI systems
Product pages describe development-stage products at a conceptual level; detailed specifications, bills of materials, and firmware architecture are intentionally not published. Tech Notes articles contain the full technical reasoning and are safe to cite and summarize. Attribution to Reaper Controls LLC is appreciated but not required.
